content: The Army Physical Fitness Test (APFT) is a standardized assessment designed to evaluate the muscular strength, endurance, and cardiovascular fitness of soldiers in the United States Army. The test consists of three events: sit-ups, push-ups, and a two-mile run. Soldiers are scored on a scale ranging from 0 to 300, with a passing score being 180 or higher. Each event requires a minimum score of 60 points to pass. The administration of the APFT and guidelines for conducting physical training sessions are outlined in Army Field Manual FM 21-20. Soldiers are required to take a record APFT every six months for official documentation. If a soldier is temporarily unable to perform one or more events due to a diagnosed medical condition, they may be granted an extension to recover and return to an acceptable level of physical fitness. However, there are no alternate events for the push-up or sit-up portions of the test. For the two-mile run, alternate events such as a two-mile bike ride may be permitted under specific circumstances. Sit-Up Event The sit-up event measures the endurance of the abdominal and hip-flexor muscles. To begin, the soldier lies on their back with knees bent at a 90-degree angle. Feet may be together or up to 12 inches apart, and another person holds the ankles using only their hands. No other bracing methods are allowed. The heels must remain in contact with the ground at all times. The soldier’s fingers must be interlocked behind the head, and the backs of the hands must touch the ground. On the command go, the soldier raises their upper body to or beyond the vertical position, defined as the base of the neck being above the base of the spine. After reaching the vertical position, the soldier lowers their body until the bottom of the shoulder blades touch the ground. The head, hands, arms, or elbows do not need to touch the ground during this phase. Repetitions are counted only if performed correctly. A repetition will not count if the soldier fails to reach the vertical position, does not keep their fingers interlocked behind the head, arches or bows their back, raises their buttocks off the ground, or allows their knees to exceed a 90-degree angle. The scorer will announce the number of correctly completed sit-ups after each repetition. Soldiers have two minutes to perform as many sit-ups as possible. The only authorized rest position is the up position. Resting in the starting position will result in termination of the event. Soldiers must make continuous physical effort to avoid disqualification. Using hands or other means to pull or push oneself into the resting position is prohibited and will result in termination of the event. Push-Up Event The push-up event measures the endurance of the chest, shoulder, and triceps muscles. Soldiers begin in the front-leaning rest position, with hands placed comfortably and feet either together or up to 12 inches apart. The body should form a generally straight line from shoulders to ankles when viewed from the side. On the command go, the soldier lowers their entire body as a single unit by bending the elbows until the upper arms are at least parallel to the ground. The soldier then returns to the starting position by fully extending the arms. The body must remain rigid and move as a single unit throughout the exercise. Repetitions are counted only if performed correctly. A repetition will not count if the soldier fails to maintain a straight body alignment, does not lower the body until the upper arms are parallel to the ground, or does not fully extend the arms. If the first ten push-ups are performed incorrectly, the scorer will stop the soldier, explain the mistakes, and send them to the end of the line for retesting. After the first ten push-ups are counted, no restarts are allowed, and any incorrectly performed push-ups will not be counted. Soldiers have two minutes to perform as many push-ups as possible. The only authorized rest position is an altered front-leaning rest position, where the soldier may sag in the middle or flex the back, but not to the extent that most body weight is supported by the legs. Resting on the ground or lifting hands or feet off the ground will result in termination of the event. Two-Mile Run The two-mile run assesses aerobic fitness and the endurance of the leg muscles. Soldiers must complete the run without any physical assistance. At the start, all participants line up behind the starting line. On the command go, the clock starts, and soldiers begin running at their own pace. The goal is to complete the two-mile course in the shortest time possible. While walking is permitted, it is strongly discouraged. Physical assistance, such as being pushed, pulled, or carried, or leaving the designated course, will result in disqualification. Pacing is allowed as long as there is no physical contact with the paced soldier and it does not hinder other participants. Cheering and calling out elapsed time are also permitted. Soldiers must ensure their identification number is visible at all times and must turn it in upon completing the run. Scoring APFT scores are based on the soldier’s sex, age, and performance in each event. For example, a 26-year-old male who completes 70 push-ups, 77 sit-ups, and runs two miles in 14:40 would receive a total score of 271 (94 points for push-ups, 96 points for sit-ups, and 81 points for the run). A minimum of 60 points in each event is required to pass the test. Soldiers who are unable to perform the two-mile run due to medical reasons may complete an alternate event, such as a walk, with a pass/fail time based on their age and sex. Their total score is calculated by averaging the push-up and sit-up scores to determine the third score. Failure to pass consecutive record APFTs can lead to separation from the Army, although this is not always the case. Soldiers who fail the APFT are often placed in a remedial program, which involves an additional daily physical training session. Failing the APFT also results in the soldier being flagged, making them ineligible for promotion, military training, or schools. However, per Army Regulation AR 600-8-2, paragraph 1-15, soldiers cannot be denied awards or decorations due to APFT failure, contrary to common misconceptions. APFT Badge Award Soldiers who score 270 or above, with a minimum of 90 points in each event, are awarded the Physical Fitness Badge, which can be worn on the physical training uniform. APFT scores also contribute to promotion points, which determine eligibility for advancement to the ranks of Sergeant (SGT) and Staff Sergeant (SSG). The scoring system includes an extended scale, allowing soldiers to earn more than 100 points in an event by exceeding the 100-point standard. To achieve a score above 300, a soldier must earn 100 points in each event before utilizing the extended scale.
